newsitem.title: PERU: Peru okays $161 mln IMF loan to finance Brady plan.
newsitem.headline: Peru okays $161 mln IMF loan to finance Brady plan.

text.p: Peru's government has approved a $160.5 million loan from the International Monetary Fund to finance some of the costs of its $4.4 billion Brady plan, according to a government decree published on Tuesday.

The loan will be used to finance some of the initial financing costs of the plan to restructure $4.4 billion of outstanding debt with creditors, the decree, carried in state- owned newspaper El Peruano said.
Peru signed the debt restructuring plan in November and hopes to complete the operation early next year.
The IMF loan, "will be re-paid over 10 years, including four and a half years grace period, through 12 quotas every six months," the decree said.
Interest charged on the loan will be equivalent to that charged by the IMF for its Special Drawing Rights, it added.
Peru's total foreign debt stood at $32.445 billion at the end of March, according to Peru's Central Bank.
